summary: Irish Gauge is a fast, cutthroat 18xx-lite game where players auction shares in five railway companies and then any shareholder can build track, upgrade towns, or call dividends for a company they hold. It plays in about an hour and rewards reading when to trigger a dividend payout versus quietly building position first.
praised: strong player interaction despite companies being jointly owned
criticised: can feel swingy or chaotic with inexperienced players
initial confusion over letting any shareholder act on a company

interaction.kind: share auction and track-building on a shared map
interaction.detail: Players build track cubes for the same five companies onto one shared map of Ireland, so a company's route and city connections are common property that affects every shareholder's dividends. Shares of each company are auctioned off one at a time, a shared pool everyone bids into, and building or upgrading a town can shape payouts for all holders of that stock, not just the acting player.

sources: final market value of held shares (based on company track/city connections)
scoring.how_you_win: Players auction and hold shares in five railway companies, build track and upgrade towns to raise dividends, and collect dividend payouts over the game; when track cubes run out or the endgame trigger hits, cash plus the sale value of held shares is totaled and the richest player wins.
